title: Tutorial: Transform a List With for
scenario: A for expression builds a new collection from an existing one. Use it to turn a list of team names into uppercase labels and a map of owners, without writing each entry twice.
constraints: Define local.teams with platform and security.
Use a for expression to build local.upper_teams.
Use a for expression to build local.team_owners.

focus.title: Derive the collections
focus.todo: Create the source list, then transform it into a list and a map.

hints.why: for expressions are the bridge between a plain collection and the shape a resource or module needs. They remove the copy-paste step that causes drift.
hints.what: Create one source list and two derived locals. One derived value is a list of uppercase names; the other is a map from each name to an owner string.
hints.when: Use a for expression when you need to transform every item in a collection. Use a map comprehension when each result needs a key.
hints.how: Start with `teams` as a list. Build `upper_teams` with a bracketed `for` expression over `local.teams` and apply the uppercase function to the loop variable. Build `team_owners` with a braced `for` expression that maps each team name to its owner string using an arrow. Keep the three local names the outputs expect.
